plugins.name: 0x
plugins.description: Guide developers through swapping ERC-20 tokens using the 0x API. Covers standard swaps via AllowanceHolder and Permit2 as well as gasless swaps across 20+ EVM chains — walking through price quotes, approvals, EIP-712 signing, and transaction submission. Also helps integrate 0x swaps directly into your app with code samples.

plugins.name: 10x-team
plugins.description:
10x-Team gives you an entire engineering team as Claude Code skills. 12 specialized roles — CTO, Product Manager, Principal Architect,
Staff Engineer, Engineering Manager, Senior Engineer, SDE, DBA, Security Engineer, QA Engineer, DevOps Engineer, and SRE — each with
structured decision processes and opinionated guidance.

Key features:

- 12 individual role skills (/cto, /architect, /sde, /security-engineer, etc.) for targeted expertise
- 1 orchestrator skill (/10x-team) that runs all 12 roles end-to-end with hard gates at every phase
- File-based project state (.10x/) so roles share decisions and track progress across conversations
- Discovery protocol that reverse-engineers existing codebases before making changes
- Every role follows a structured process — no generic advice, only actionable recommendations with trade-offs
- Brainstorm-first approach — the orchestrator won't let you write code until the design is validated

plugins.name: 16minds
plugins.description:
16-minds summons agents modeled on 16 distinct personality types — each with its own values, thinking patterns, and tone — to debate, review, or advise on any topic. Each personality is written directly into an independent prompt, so outputs carry visibly different voices instead of the averaged answer a single agent tends to produce.

Three commands cover the range:
  - /mind <type> — a single type's opinion
  - /pair <a> <b> — a two-type debate (open → rebut → reply / synthesize)
  - /minds — fan out to all 16 in parallel, then synthesize

Three modes (light / middle / heavy) trade depth for token cost.

The /minds synthesis follows a fixed 4-section rubric — score distribution, axes of disagreement, easily-overlooked perspectives, and landing-zone candidates with per-candidate "types likely to agree / fit / risk" — to keep 16-voice output structured rather than scattershot. The --save flag writes the full execution log to a file for use as article material or decision logs.

Built for decisions where a single averaged answer would lose the edges: idea generation, design judgment, code review, and life/career questions.
